findings.issue: Inside each operator loop the current id is re-read as a memory slice `Bytes(24, 0), mem[... len 8]` (P18) and the whole slice expression is repeated as a one-element `concat` key (P4) in every access to the operator struct, making 300-character lines; `Mask(192, 64, uint32(x))` is always 0 and the check it guards can never fire.
findings.rule: Read an 8-byte slice ending a 32-byte word as `uint64(word)`, bind the loop's current element to a variable, print `stor[sha3(k, base)]` with a single-word key as `map[k]`; fold masks of values whose width is known to be smaller than the mask offset.

notes: Seven large via-IR functions (200-600 lines each) reviewed by structure. All 10 source loops are shown as whiles: MerkleProof.processProof (`while t < _63`), OperatorLib.updateClusterOperators / ...Migration / ...OnReactivation / ...SSV, _updateOperatorVUnits, _liquidateAfterEBUpdateIfNeeded, _executeLiquidation, and the loops in withdraw and migrateClusterToETH; they all look alike (`while idx < cd[_param + 4]: require not Mask(192, 64, cd[s])`), the per-iteration range check being real because operatorIds is `uint64[] calldata`. Implicit: the abi.encodePacked copies of operatorIds for the cluster hash (validate-and-copy, then `Bytes(24, 0), mem[s + 24 len 8]` re-encoding, P7). P6: 44 lines with 63-digit words. No semantic error found.
summary: Faithful, abort-free text with all 10 operator/Merkle loops as whiles; readability is poor because the current operator id is repeated as a long memory-slice concat key in every struct access.
